# Framework fixture — no-common-endpoint mode

The fixture contains three research types: a catalytic experiment reporting isolated yield (F-001, p. 2 Table 1), a docking study reporting a binding score (F-002, p. 6 Figure 4), and a materials aging study reporting retention after cycling (F-007, p. 8 Table 1). They do not share a defensible endpoint, denominator, or experimental context.

- **Evidence map:** F-001 answers a local synthesis-performance question; F-002 answers a computational binding hypothesis; F-007 answers a device-aging question.
- **Research typology:** experimental reaction outcome, in silico interaction score, and device durability measurement.
- **Local explanation chain:** within F-001, ligand/context can be connected to isolated yield; within F-007, processing history can be connected to cycling retention. No cross-type chain is asserted.
- **Boundary:** F-001 versus F-002 and F-007 versus F-002 are `NOT_COMPARABLE`; differences in endpoint and context prevent ranking.
- **Chemical GAP:** a common benchmark or bridge experiment would be needed before a cross-domain claim could be tested.

No unified ranking is produced. This is a useful Framework result even though a single global score cannot be defended.
